Author: DJ Daniels
Message:
fix(talos): enable age-based image GC — nothing was pruning container images

Talos ships kubelet with imageMaximumGCAge: 0s, so image garbage collection is purely a
disk-pressure reflex. Nothing prunes by age; images accumulate without bound until a node
crosses imageGCHighThresholdPercent 85, then kubelet dumps to 80 in one uncontrolled sweep.

Measured 2026-08-24:
    talos06      763 / 929 Gi   82%   2,504 images, 306 unreferenced (~261 GB) since APRIL
    talos02-gpu  663 / 1905 Gi  35%
    every node growing ~2 GB/day since 2026-08-09

talos06 was three points from that uncontrolled sweep and ten from the evictionHard
nodefs.available=10% line added earlier the same day.

The two media nodes are worst because they have the most image churn, which is exactly why
this looked like unpruned GPU/transcode cache. It is not — it is container images. The
transcode theory would have sent the fix to entirely the wrong place.

336h (14 days) is long enough that anything in normal rotation, including weekly CronJobs
and workloads that idle between runs, is never collected. Safe for live workloads:
imageMaximumGCAge counts from LAST USE and an image pinned by a running container is never
a candidate regardless of age. It will evict images for workloads scaled to zero that are
expected to return — those re-pull on scale-up, which costs a pull, not data.

Applied to all five nodes without reboot (kubelet restart only), verified
336h0m0s via /proc configz on each. Added to bootstrap-talos-patches.sh so rebuilt nodes
inherit it.

Root cause for TALOS-2ome; enables the ~260 GB/node reclaim in TALOS-cd73.

Author: DJ Daniels
Message:
fix(traefik): lock down the dashboard/API — HTTPS + auth, off the plaintext :80 (TALOS-lxz5.1.1)

The Traefik dashboard and api@internal were served unauthenticated on the `web` (:80)
entrypoint with `--api.insecure=true`, and a 2026-09 red-team confirmed GET /api/rawdata
returned 200 (full config, 413 routers) from the public internet via Host-header spoof.

- Remove `--api.insecure=true` (keep `--api.dashboard=true`; api@internal still backs the route).
- Move the dashboard IngressRoute from `web` to `websecure`, gated by `lan-only` + `authentik`
  forward-auth (defense in depth, mirroring the crowdsec.talos00 admin-UI pattern).

Paired security-posture tests (scripts/security/test_security_posture.py):
  - test_traefik_api_insecure_disabled (offline)
  - test_traefik_dashboard_off_plaintext_and_authenticated (offline)

Author: DJ Daniels
Message:
fix(talos): enable age-based image GC — nothing was pruning container images

Talos ships kubelet with imageMaximumGCAge: 0s, so image garbage collection is purely a
disk-pressure reflex. Nothing prunes by age; images accumulate without bound until a node
crosses imageGCHighThresholdPercent 85, then kubelet dumps to 80 in one uncontrolled sweep.

Measured 2026-08-24:
    talos06      763 / 929 Gi   82%   2,504 images, 306 unreferenced (~261 GB) since APRIL
    talos02-gpu  663 / 1905 Gi  35%
    every node growing ~2 GB/day since 2026-08-09

talos06 was three points from that uncontrolled sweep and ten from the evictionHard
nodefs.available=10% line added earlier the same day.

The two media nodes are worst because they have the most image churn, which is exactly why
this looked like unpruned GPU/transcode cache. It is not — it is container images. The
transcode theory would have sent the fix to entirely the wrong place.

336h (14 days) is long enough that anything in normal rotation, including weekly CronJobs
and workloads that idle between runs, is never collected. Safe for live workloads:
imageMaximumGCAge counts from LAST USE and an image pinned by a running container is never
a candidate regardless of age. It will evict images for workloads scaled to zero that are
expected to return — those re-pull on scale-up, which costs a pull, not data.

Applied to all five nodes without reboot (kubelet restart only), verified
336h0m0s via /proc configz on each. Added to bootstrap-talos-patches.sh so rebuilt nodes
inherit it.

Root cause for TALOS-2ome; enables the ~260 GB/node reclaim in TALOS-cd73.

Author: DJ Daniels
Message:
refactor(home-assistant): CNPG via static config, drop brittle init-container db_url munging (TALOS-hx77.1)

The prior approach patched configuration.yaml at boot (heredoc + sed from a secret env);
it silently wrote an empty db_url and HA fell back to SQLite. Replace with the native,
declarative pattern: recorder db_url is static in the ConfigMap pointing at the CNPG
homeassistant-postgres-rw service, and the app-user password is PINNED via a pre-created
secret adopted by CNPG (bootstrap.initdb.secret) so no runtime templating is needed. Init
container reduced to first-run seed + !include file touch. No config is rewritten at runtime.

Principle: prefer native config over brittle init-container abstractions.

Author: DJ Daniels
Message:
fix(authentik): full IaC blueprint for litellm OIDC SSO chain

The previous blueprint failed validation with "No or invalid identifiers"
because it used a top-level `id:` field instead of the required
`identifiers:` mapping. In Authentik blueprints, `id:` is only an internal
reference handle for `!KeyOf`, while `identifiers:` is the
how-to-find-or-create lookup. Without it, the entry is rejected.

Rewrites the blueprint to provision the entire SSO chain so it survives
cluster rebuilds:
  1. Group         litellm-admins (empty by default)
  2. ScopeMapping  litellm_role -> proxy_admin / internal_user
  3. OAuth2Provider litellm (confidential, pinned client_id/secret)
  4. Application   litellm (slug=litellm, bound to the provider)

client_id/client_secret are pinned so a fresh Authentik DB recreates the
exact credentials already stored in 1Password and consumed by the LiteLLM
container via litellm-secrets (oidc-client-id / oidc-client-secret).

Verified on cluster: BlueprintInstance status=successful, all 4 objects
present, client_secret matches the live value.

Author: DJ Daniels
Message:
feat(home-automation): add postgres for HA recorder, migrate off NFS SQLite

Deploy a dedicated postgres:15-alpine instance in home-automation namespace

- Updated deployment.yaml: init-container patches recorder config on existing
  installs, liveness probe tightened (was 180s/60s/10, now 120s/30s/5)
- Updated kustomization.yaml: include postgres.yaml
